prompt: Stream.distinct() only compares whole elements, so write distinctByKey(keyFn): a Predicate that remembers the keys it has seen, then use it to keep the first email address per domain.
explanation: A Set's add method returns true only when the value was not already present, which is exactly the "first time I have seen this" answer a filter needs. Declaring the Set outside the lambda and capturing it makes the returned Predicate stateful, and because a fresh Set is created on every call to distinctByKey each pipeline gets its own memory. Lowercasing the domain before it becomes the key is what makes "Mail.com" and "mail.COM" collapse together while the original addresses are returned untouched.
hints: Set.add(x) returns true when x was NOT already in the set -- that boolean is the whole predicate.
Create the HashSet inside distinctByKey but OUTSIDE the lambda, so the lambda captures it and it survives across calls.
For the domain key, find indexOf('@'); if it is negative use "", otherwise substring(at + 1).toLowerCase().
